headline: Denied a zero-frontage variance on Bonanno Court on a 3-1 vote; approved a fence waiver at 225 Pelham Street.
summary: Melissa Ansara-Burns & Michael Burns received approval for a 6 ft. privacy fence set 3.5 feet from the Harvard Avenue lot line. Kerri Dimauro, represented by attorney Arthur Broadhurst, asked for a variance to build a house on a landlocked lot on Bonanno Court with a 20-foot driveway easement. The variance failed because approval required a unanimous vote of all four members, and the plot plan also listed the wrong city.
decisions: Approved a fence ordinance waiver for a 6 ft. privacy fence at 225 Pelham Street, 4-0.
Denied a zero-frontage variance on Bonanno Court, 3-1.

TRANSCRIPT OF PUBLIC RECORD 
ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS MEETING 
September 23, 2026 
 
This Regular Meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals, was held in The Great Hall, 41 Pleasant Street, Methuen 
MA. The meeting was called to order at: 7:00 PM.   
 
Vice Chairman Nicholas Boucher, presided as “Acting Chairman” and asked for a moment of silence in memory 
for all those who have died for our country, and led the pledge of allegiance.  
 
MEMBERS IN ATTENDANCE: 
Mr. Nicholas Boucher, Acting Chairman 
Mr. Philip Cultrera, Member 
Mr. William Haneffant, Alternate Member 
Mr. Mr. Mansour Chaya, Alternate Member 
 
Also, In Attendance: 
Joseph Salamone, Building Commissioner 
Lori Moriarty HHSI Clerk III 
Petitioners and Representatives 
 
MEMBERS ABSENT: 
Mr. Matteo Zingales, Member 
Mr. Jose Frias, Clerk 
Mr. Vincenzo Pesce, Member 
 
Acting Chair, Nicholas Boucher, read the following statement and asked for a motion to enter into executive 
session, which was followed by a roll call vote.  
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION: 
The Zoning Board of Appeals will vote to enter into Executive Session, with legal counsel for the 
Board, in accordance with Exemption 7 (Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 30A, Section 21(a)(7)), 
in order to discuss recent changes to the Zoning Act. After the conclusion of the Executive Session, the 
Zoning Board of Appeals will reconvene in Open Session. 
 
Motion: Philip Cultrera 
Second: Mansour Chaya 
 
ROLL CALL VOTE:  
Mr. Nicholas Boucher- Yes 
Mr. William Haneffant- Yes 
Mr. Mr. Mansour Chaya- Yes 
Mr. Philip Cultrera- Yes 
 
OPEN SESSION: 
Open session resumed at 7:24PM
Page 2 of 4 
 
ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES: 
• August 26, 2026 
 
Mansour Chaya made a motion to accept the minutes of August 26, 2026.  Phil Cultrera seconded.  
DISCUSSION: NONE 
VOTE: UNANIMOUS  
 
ROLL OF APPLICANTS:  
 Melissa Ansara-Burns & Michael Burns - present 
Kerri Dimauro represented by Attorney Arthur Broadhurst - present  
 
NEW BUSINESS: 
 
Request for Fence Ordinance Waiver: 
 
2026-13 Melissa Ansara-Burns & Michael Burns 
A fence ordinance waiver is required under chapter 9, Section 9-89 of the Municipal Code 
of Methuen (Ordinance Regulating Fences) for a 6 ft. privacy fence within a front yard 
along Harvard Ave. The required setback in the RB zone is 25 feet, but the requested 
setback is 3.5 feet from the lot line along Harvard Ave. at  225 Pelham Street, Methuen 
MA 01844 (Parcel ID: 412-126A-69A).  
 
Michael and Melissa Burns came to the Podium, from 225 Pelham St. They are seeking a Fence Ordinance 
Waiver.  Acting Chair Boucher opened up the floor for the Board to ask questions. 
 
Phil Cultrera stated that he noticed an approval sign off by officer Hatem, of Methuen PD, making sure there 
won’t be any traffic view obstructions with their fence plan, turning left and right on Harvard Ave.  He asked 
the applicant if they would be following the existing fence in the rear, and continue it around.   The petitioners 
stated that they would be and purchased the home in 2012. There was a picket fence in need of repair when they 
purchased and they will be putting the fence in the same place. 
 
Bill Haneffant asked where about the fence would be ending, coming from the back to the intersection. The 
petitioner stated it would be about 20-25 feet from Pelham Street, it will stop where the house starts.  Nick 
Boucher asked if that was where the previous fence was, and the petitioner confirmed it is.  
 
Acting Chair Boucher opened Public participation.  No one came forward either in favor or in opposition.  
The Chairman closed Public participation and asked for a roll call vote.  
 
ROLL CALL VOTE:   
 
Nicholas Boucher: yes 
William Haneffant: yes 
Mansour Chaya: yes 
Mr. Philip Cultrera: yes 
 
The Fence Ordinance waiver has been approved. 
 
Application for Variance: 
 
2026-14 Kerri Dimauro represented by Attorney Arthur Broadhurst
Page 3 of 4 
 
A Variance for lot frontage is required per APPENDIX B TABLE OF DIMENSIONAL 
REGULATIONS of the May 2025 City of Methuen Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance in 
a RD (Single-Family Residence District. The required minimum is 100-feet and the 
requested is zero-feet, at (VP) Bonanno Court, Methuen MA 01844 (Parcel ID: 1210-
110B-16FF).  
 
Attorney Arthur Broadhurst, with offices at 45 Osgood St. Methuen, came forward representing the petitioner 
and owners of the property.  The owners currently have an existing property with a house on it and a vacant lot 
behind it, which is landlocked. The Current owner wants to provide their granddaughter the ability to build a 
house on the landlocked property with a driveway easement. The plan would meet all other dimensional 
requirements except frontage.  They are seeking variance relief for the zero-frontage lot.  Attorney Broadhurst 
stated he believed the newly passed zoning laws, 40A, from the State, would fit into this lot plan.  The Board 
can weigh the benefit of the public interest related to housing.  The petitioners are a young couple, who would 
be given an opportunity to build a house on a lot not being used.  Attorney Broadhurst stated that the Board 
could find a financial hardship to both the new owner and current owner, maintaining existing homes are not 
affordable, and they have a lot they can only use as a yard.  Attorney Broadhurst also stated that this would 
bring the City more tax revenue. Attorney Broadhurst advised the Board they are allowed to consider affordable 
housing in their decision.  A 20ft easement would be needed for driveway, which could be conditioned as part 
of the variance.  
 
Acting Chair Boucher opened up the floor for questions from the Board.  
 
Mansour Chaya stated that other landlocked parcels in the area do not have any houses on them.  He asked if 
this proposed driveway easement would be used for those other landlocked properties as well as this lot.  
Attorney Broadhurst stated that the other abutting landlocked properties were not part of this plan.  
 
Mr. Chaya asked about the two properties being owned by the same owner and how that would relate to current 
zoning laws. Attorney Broadhurst stated that there used to be a doctrine of merging that merged properties 
automatically, and he stated that has been done away with as part of this new law.  Attorney Broadhurst said 
that they have not been notified from the building department, as part of the denial, that a form A subdivision 
plan is needed, but they will file one with Community Development if necessary.  
 
Phil Cultrera asked if the proposal is for a colonial style house, and Attorney Broadhurst confirmed it was.   
 
Nick Boucher stated that there is an error with the application, and that the plot plan is incorrect.  It lists the 
subject site as 64 Bonanno Ct. in Andover MA.  
 
Attorney Broadhurst stated that he didn’t notice the error and that he can have the engineer fix it tomorrow, and 
submit it to the Board. The firm is Andover Consultants, and he speculated that may be what led to the error.   
 
There were no other questions from the Board.  
 
The Acting Chair opened public participation.  Several extended family members were in attendance and 
showed by hands that they were in favor.  No one came forward to provide name or addresses, although the 
Acting Chair gave the opportunity to do so.    No one came forward in opposition and public participation was 
closed.  
 
Acting Chair Boucher stated that there is only 4 members of the Board available and that a vote would require a 
unanimous decision of all 4 members approve.  He gave the applicant the opportunity to continue to the next
Page 4 of 4 
 
public hearing.  Attorney Broadhurst stated that he spoke with his client about it, and they want to move 
forward with a vote tonight. 
 
Attorney Broadhurst confirmed again that he can cross out the wrong City on the Plot plan and initial it and get 
the new plans to the Board the following day.  He also stated that if this would cause a “no” vote, he would then 
ask for a continuance.   
 
Nick Boucher stated that they will move forward with the vote and pending the outcome they would accept the 
edited documents.  
 
Nick Boucher stated that he does not like the idea of zero frontage, and he hasn’t approved that in the past. He 
said he likes to be consistent with his vote.  The fact that the paperwork was not correct was not a deciding 
factor in his vote.   
 
ROLL CALL VOTE:   
 
Nicholas Boucher: No 
William Haneffant: Yes 
Mansour Chaya: Yes 
Phil Cultrera: Yes 
 
 
ADJOURNMENT: 
 
There being no further business before the Board , Phil Cultrera made a motion to adjourn, and Bill Haneffant 
seconded. 
Discussion: None 
 Vote: Unanimous 
 
Acting Chairman Nicholas Boucher adjourned the meeting at 7:38 PM. 
 
Respectfully Submitted, 
Lori Moriarty 
City Clerk III HHSI
